prompt: Some people believe that people have the right to university education, and government should make it free no matter what their financial background. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
essay:
Many people argue that access to university education is a fundamental right and that governments should provide it free of charge to all citizens, regardless of their financial situation. I partly agree with this view because higher education brings sizeable benefits both to individuals and to society. However, I do not believe that completely free university education for everyone is always the most effective or realistic solution.

On the one hand, making university education free can create equal opportunities for people from different social backgrounds. Talented students from low-income families often struggle to pay for tuition fees, which may prevent them from reaching their full potential. If higher education were funded by the government, more students could obtain professional qualifications and contribute to the economy. In addition, a well-educated population generally leads to lower unemployment rates, higher productivity, and greater innovation, all of which benefit society as a whole.

On the other hand, providing free university education to every student would require enormous public expenditure. Governments have limited budgets and must also fund healthcare, infrastructure, and social well-being programs. In some cases, it may be unfair for taxpayers to fully finance the education of students who come from wealthy families and can easily afford tuition fees. Furthermore, when education is completely free, some students may not value it as much as those who have invested financially in their studies.

In conclusion, although I strongly support the idea that everyone should have access to university education, I do not completely agree that it should be free for all citizens regardless of their financial background. A targeted support system for students in need would be a more practical and equitable policy.
